reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary content is a hosted interview about Avalanche Treasury Co., AVAX strategy, and digital-asset treasury structures. A separately identified Uphold segment presents crypto rewards, recurring deposit, and trading conditions as sponsorship with terms and a capital-risk disclosure. The investment topics are framed as interview discussion, including a statement that no market-capitalization forecast is being made.

citations.quote: Why this Avalanche AVAX Digital Asset Treasury Company is a Game Changer!
Bart Smith, who is the CEO and chairman of the avalanche Treasury Co.
this episode is brought to you by uphold
you can earn up to 5.25% on stable coins
to participate, you just simply have to open the app once per month, deposit $50 once per month, and trade $50 once per month.

opening.argument: Judge, the Uphold segment does more than name a sponsor. It offers a specific reward rate, gives viewers a recurring checklist of app use, deposits and trades, then directs them to the description link. That is a reward tied to repeated financial action, embedded in a video that viewers may have opened for an interview. The question is not whether the rate is guaranteed; it is whether the reward claim is being used to move viewers into a deposit-and-trade routine.

citations.quote: you can earn up to 5.25% on stable coins.
to participate, you just simply have to open the app once per month, deposit $50 once per month, and trade $50 once per month.
visit the link in the description.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a separately identified sponsorship does not break the link between the reward and the requested actions. The cited monthly conditions require deposits and trades, not just listening to an interview. Nor does saying that terms apply establish what those terms do to the advertised reward.

citations.quote: deposit $50 once per month, and trade $50 once per month.
Signup with Uphold. https://uphold.sjv.io/gbED4X Terms Apply.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The segment openly identifies Uphold as its sponsor, and the description states both that terms apply and that cryptoassets put capital at risk. A conditional rewards offer with a disclosed signup link does not, by itself, establish that the reward is fictitious or that viewers are deceived.

citations.quote: this episode is brought to you by uphold
Terms Apply. Cryptoassets are highly volatile. Your capital is at risk.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The sponsor segment advertises stablecoin rewards and crypto staking, while the host offers an assurance about the platform's safety and reserves. The same segment sends interested viewers to a link, and the description warns that cryptoassets are highly volatile. The concern is the combined impression: a return opportunity is made to feel dependable through a personal endorsement, even though the supplied material does not independently verify the platform claims or show how the stated risks affect the advertised rewards.

citations.quote: they offer a crypto staking on over 19 crypto assets.
You can earn up to 5% on that stable coin and 5.25% on USB-C
I've been a user of the platform for many years, they are safe and reliable, they don't commingle or lend out your crypto funds, and they are 100% reserved.
Cryptoassets are highly volatile. Your capital is at risk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The interview's lack of a market-capitalization forecast does not address the sponsor's concrete reward rates. Identifying the sponsorship tells viewers who paid for the segment; it does not substantiate the host's claims that the platform is safe, reliable and fully reserved.

citations.quote: You can earn up to 5% on that stable coin and 5.25% on USB-C
they are safe and reliable, they don't commingle or lend out your crypto funds, and they are 100% reserved.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An endorsement is not independent proof, but its presence is not proof of deception either. The reward language says 'up to,' the description says terms apply, and it expressly warns of volatility and capital risk. The cited material gives no basis to conclude that the advertised rewards are unavailable or that the reserve claim is false.

citations.quote: you can earn up to 5.25% on stable coins.
Terms Apply. Cryptoassets are highly volatile. Your capital is at risk.

opening.argument: Judge, the interview format also carries an investment pitch. The title calls the AVAX treasury company a 'Game Changer,' the host discloses that he holds AVAX, and the guest describes raising public-market capital to pursue more AVAX per share for shareholders. Those are not merely abstract observations about an asset class; they present a favorable investment thesis from people with a stated stake or role in it. The conversational format can make the proposed shareholder upside feel like independent analysis, while the cited remarks do not establish that the strategy will produce it.

citations.quote: Why this Avalanche AVAX Digital Asset Treasury Company is a Game Changer!
I'm an AVAX token holder. So I'm excited to get into the details.
you can raise money in you know in the public markets in a variety of ways
trying to generate more AVAX per share for our shareholders.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that this is a hosted interview, but that format does not make its favorable framing neutral. The host's disclosed AVAX holding and the guest's stated shareholder objective give a judge reason to scrutinize the promotional effect. The absence of a market-capitalization forecast does not substantiate the proposed increase in AVAX per share.

citations.quote: I'm an AVAX token holder. So I'm excited to get into the details.
trying to generate more AVAX per share for our shareholders.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The host discloses his AVAX holding rather than concealing it. The guest describes a goal, not an assured gain, and explicitly says he has no market-capitalization forecast. The interview also discusses the possibility of a meaningful, prolonged sell-off. Promotional enthusiasm alone does not turn this discussion into evidence of a deceptive token-purchase offer.

citations.quote: I'm an AVAX token holder.
I don't have any forecasts of where the market capitalization is going to go.
that could be a pretty meaningful sell-off and it could last for a long time.
